goal.statement: Software teams without prior AI experience can move from product discussion to a shared, understandable product narrative and first useful delivery slice substantially faster.

peopleConsidered.note: A named human confirmed that they considered who else is relevant for the goal. That is what they did; it does not say the people on the map are complete.

value.note: The slice references at least one need on the map. ASM has not measured any business value.

whyThisSlice: The last step “Export execution-ready work” (step-export-work) serves need-buildable-slice, need-stable-references; this slice is every step that serves one of those needs.
Primary persona relevance: Product Lead / Product Owner (persona-product-lead) takes part in 3 of the 4 included steps.
Persona overlap: 2 of the 4 included steps involve more than one persona.
Need relation: serves 4 of 7 needs (need-shared-narrative, need-approve-meaning, need-buildable-slice, need-stable-references).
Main-path completeness: reaches the end of the main path, “Export execution-ready work”.
Scope: 4 of 12 main-path steps, with 2 worst-case branch(es) to handle.
assumptions: Assumes “Start product” [step-start-product] has already happened outside this slice.
Assumes the steps skipped between included steps are done by hand: [step-add-wcbc] [step-review-gaps] [step-approve-narrative] [step-walk-through-the-slice-with-the-team].
Assumes the included needs contribute to the goal [goal-faster-shared-narrative]; the map relates steps to needs, not needs to the goal.

decidedDecisions.title: The canonical product model is a YAML file inside the repository
decidedDecisions.rationale: Given by the slice brief (no database, no graph server). A file is diffable, reviewable and readable by agents.

decidedDecisions.title: Visual position is never the sole source of semantics
decidedDecisions.rationale: Narrative order lives in an explicit sequence field and relations in ids. Layout is stored separately and can change without touching meaning.

decidedDecisions.title: Only an explicit human action approves a revision
decidedDecisions.rationale: Narrative-first means humans define intent and approve meaning. Saving or editing never approves anything.

approvedContext.note: Approved means a named human approved the narrative. ASM has verified nothing: no behaviour described here has been built or tested.

inScope.title: Build main / best-case path
inScope.description: The main narrative is laid out as an ordered sequence of steps.

branches.title: Main path reads as one story
branches.description: A newcomer can follow the narrative from start to export without explanation.

inScope.title: Review first slice candidates
inScope.description: Candidate first slices through the approved narrative are compared.

inScope.title: Human selects first slice
inScope.description: A human picks the first slice to deliver.

branches.title: No candidate slice is small enough
branches.description: Every candidate is too large to be a first delivery.
branches.recovery: Return to the main path and cut a thinner slice through it.

inScope.title: Export execution-ready work
inScope.description: The selected slice leaves ASM in a form a delivery team can execute.

branches.title: Exported file fails validation on import
branches.description: A product file was changed by hand and no longer validates.
branches.recovery: Validation names the exact path of each issue; an invalid file is never written.

outOfScope: [step-walk-through-the-slice-with-the-team] Walk through the slice with the team
[need-real-situations] Need not served by this slice: See real user situations, including failure and recovery, represented in the narrative.
[need-see-gaps] Need not served by this slice: Spot gaps and unresolved decisions before anything is built on them.
[need-trace-a-customer-problem-back-to-the-nar] Need not served by this slice: Trace a customer problem back to the narrative step it belongs to.

personas.name: Product Lead / Product Owner
personas.description: Owns product intent and approves what the narrative means.

personas.name: Domain or UX Expert
personas.description: Knows the real user situations, including where things go wrong.

personas.name: Developer
personas.description: Turns the approved narrative into a first delivery slice.

needs.statement: Turn a product discussion into one narrative the whole team understands, without prior AI experience.
Remain the one who approves meaning; nothing counts as agreed until I approve it.
Receive a first slice that is small, unambiguous and ready to execute.
Rely on stable ids and explicit relations rather than on where a card happens to sit.

acceptanceCriteriaDraft.text: [step-main-path] Product Lead / Product Owner / Domain or UX Expert / Developer can complete “Build main / best-case path”: The main narrative is laid out as an ordered sequence of steps.
[step-review-slices] Product Lead / Product Owner / Developer can complete “Review first slice candidates”: Candidate first slices through the approved narrative are compared.
[step-select-slice] Product Lead / Product Owner can complete “Human selects first slice”: A human picks the first slice to deliver.
[wcbc-no-small-slice] When “No candidate slice is small enough”, then: Return to the main path and cut a thinner slice through it.
[step-export-work] Developer can complete “Export execution-ready work”: The selected slice leaves ASM in a form a delivery team can execute.
[wcbc-export-invalid] When “Exported file fails validation on import”, then: Validation names the exact path of each issue; an invalid file is never written.

verificationExpectations.expectation: Show step-main-path working for each named persona with a recorded run (test output or screen recording), not a description.
Show step-review-slices working for each named persona with a recorded run (test output or screen recording), not a description.
Show step-select-slice working for each named persona with a recorded run (test output or screen recording), not a description.
Provoke the situation of wcbc-no-small-slice and show, with a recorded run, that what follows matches the criterion.
Show step-export-work working for each named persona with a recorded run (test output or screen recording), not a description.
Provoke the situation of wcbc-export-invalid and show, with a recorded run, that what follows matches the criterion.

openHumanDecisions.text: What does "substantially faster" mean in measurable terms?
What makes a slice candidate a "first useful" slice?
What form does "execution-ready work" take on export?
Worst case “Exported file fails validation on import” does not say where it leads: no recovery step, termination or escalation is referenced.
